💬 Large Language Models (LLMs)

What is Generative AI?

AI that creates new content — not just classifies or predicts.

📝 Text

Essays, lesson plans, emails, quiz questions

🖼️ Images

Illustrations, diagrams, visual aids

🎵 Audio

Narration, music, language pronunciation

🎬 Video

Explainer videos, animated content

How Do LLMs Work?

"LLMs are like highly knowledgeable autocomplete systems trained on enormous amounts of text."
  • They predict the next most likely word
  • Trained on billions of web pages, books & articles
  • They don't "understand" — they pattern-match
  • This is why they can be confidently wrong

4️⃣ AI Terminology — Simplified

Words every teacher should know

⏱️ 10 minutes

Key Vocabulary

Prompt — The instruction you give to AI

Context — Background info you provide

Context Window — How much AI can "remember" in a chat

Tokens — Small chunks of words AI processes

Hallucination — AI confidently giving wrong info

Temperature — Controls creativity vs accuracy

RAG — AI using trusted docs before answering

Token Billing — Why some tools charge by usage

Real-World Example

Context in Action

"I teach Grade 8 Science in CBSE. Create a worksheet on photosynthesis with diagrams and fill-in-the-blanks."

↑ This prompt has: Role Context Task Format

The more context you provide, the better the output.

5️⃣ Prompt Engineering for Teachers

The #1 skill that makes AI useful

⏱️ 15 minutes

Bad Prompt vs Good Prompt

❌ Bad Prompt

"Create a lesson plan on fractions."

✅ Good Prompt

"Create a Grade 5 CBSE mathematics lesson plan on fractions. Include learning objectives, classroom activities, group exercises, assessment questions, and differentiation for advanced learners."

The R-C-T-F Framework

🎭 R — Role Who should AI act as?

📚 C — Context Teaching environment, board, grade

📝 T — Task What needs to be done?

📄 F — Format How should the output look?

Remember: R-C-T-F = Better prompts = Better outputs

Prompt Upgrade Example

"Make a quiz"

⬇️

"Make a quiz on gravity for Class 9"

⬇️

"You are an experienced CBSE physics teacher. Create a 15-question quiz on gravity for Class 9 students. Include 5 MCQs, 5 short-answer, and 5 HOTS questions. Provide an answer key with marking scheme. Format as a printable worksheet."

💡 Advanced Prompting Tips

  • Chain of thought — Ask AI to "think step by step"
  • Few-shot examples — Show AI what you want with examples
  • Iterate — Refine: "Make it simpler" / "Add more detail"
  • Specify constraints — "Use only 200 words" / "Bloom's Taxonomy Level 4"
  • Assign a persona — "Act as a child psychologist" / "You are a curriculum designer"

8️⃣ Risks, Limitations & Responsible AI

What every educator must know

⏱️ 5 minutes

⚠️ Key Risks

🎭 Hallucinations

AI can invent facts, quotes, citations, and even research papers that don't exist.

Always verify!

⚖️ Bias

AI inherits biases from its training data — cultural, gender, and socioeconomic biases can appear.

Review critically!

🔒 Privacy

Never share student names, marks, personal data, or school-sensitive info with public AI tools.

©️ Copyright

AI-generated content may resemble copyrighted material. Use it as a starting point, not the final product.

🛡️ Golden Rules for Safe AI Use

  • AI is your assistant, not your replacement
  • Always verify facts and information
  • Never share personal or sensitive student data
  • Review & edit every AI output before using it
  • Understand your school's data privacy policy

9️⃣ Students & AI

Opportunities, challenges & what teachers can do

⏱️ 10 minutes

Benefits for Students

  • 🎓 Personalised tutoring — AI explains at the student's pace
  • 🔍 Faster research — Quick summaries and explanations
  • 🌐 Language support — Translation and simplification
  • 💡 Better explanations — "Explain like I'm 10 years old"

Challenges & Concerns

  • 📋 Homework outsourcing — Students submitting AI work as their own
  • 🧠 Reduced critical thinking — Over-reliance on AI answers
  • 📄 Plagiarism — Difficult to detect AI-written text
  • 🔗 Overdependence — Students unable to work without AI

⚠️ No AI detection tool is 100% accurate!

✅ Better Approaches

Instead of trying to catch AI use, redesign assessments:

  • Process-based assessment — Evaluate drafts, not just finals
  • Oral defence / viva — Ask students to explain their work
  • In-class writing — Supervised, no-device assessments
  • Project journals — Document the learning journey
  • Application-based questions — Require real-world context
  • Collaborative work — Peer discussions that AI can't replicate

🔟 AI Policy for Schools

Building a responsible framework

⏱️ 5 minutes

Suggested Guidelines

✅ Teachers Should

  • Use AI for lesson preparation & productivity
  • Always verify AI outputs before classroom use
  • Use AI as an assistant, not a replacement
  • Stay updated on new tools & best practices

Student Guidelines

✅ Students May

  • Use AI for brainstorming & idea generation
  • Use AI as a study tutor
  • Cite AI assistance when required
  • Use AI for language support

🚫 Students Should Not

  • Submit AI-generated work as their own
  • Use AI during restricted assessments
  • Share personal data with AI tools
  • Rely on AI without verification
